screen: Claim 3 — client-review chrome, 11 edges replayed
finding: Three of the four numbers reproduce — 4 masters, 39 instances, 0 local copies. The fourth does not: 8 replayed edges survive, not 11. Three were destroyed by the replay loop itself.
evidence: Page 1:6 defines 4 masters: COMPONENT_SET 2059:7457 'Client / Branded bar' (2 variants), COMPONENT_SET 2059:7483 'Client / Sticky footer' (4 variants), COMPONENT 2059:7465 'Client / Mode strip', COMPONENT 2059:7487 'Client / Agency header'. Instances of those 4 = 39 (Branded bar 16, Mode strip 10, Sticky footer 10, Agency header 3). Local copies matching /branded bar|mode strip|sticky footer|agency header/ = 0. Every instance matches its master variant size exactly (16x 1280x56, 10x 1280x44, 10x 1280x72, 3x 1280x56) — no clipping. Root-level override edges on those 39 instances = 8, on 8 distinct bars: landing-viewing Mode strip->114:2 and Sticky footer->117:58; A0-returning-visitor the same two; commenting Mode strip->23:21 and Sticky footer->117:58; request-changes Sticky footer->122:3; brand-colour Sticky footer->117:58. Mechanism is provable from scripts/figma/swap-client-chrome.mjs:75-83 — 'for (const dest of edges) { await inst.setReactionsAsync([{ ...one action... }]); replayed++ }'. setReactionsAsync REPLACES the node's reactions, so a bar carrying N captured edges increments the counter N times and ends with exactly 1. 11 increments over 8 bars = 3 edges lost.
recommend: Re-derive the lost 3 from git history of the pre-swap page, or accept 8 and re-wire by hand. Fix the loop before it is reused: build the full actions array first, then call setReactionsAsync once.

Zero full-shell boards in: Brand (35), History (26), Layers (18), Content (22), Pages (16), Publish (14), Insert (13), AI (11), Inspector (26), Compare (8), Review (23), Client sign-off (10), Notifications (6), Command palette (7), Preview (7), Canvas (10), Ecommerce (5) — 257 boards across 17 modules. It is nine boards and it is the only way a reviewer can compare rail alignment, drawer width and panel-header height between modules by looking rather than by measuring.

screen: C — the Inspector colour row disagrees with itself
finding: On the Inspector TEXT profile, the Color row draws a blue swatch next to the value '#1A1A1A'. The swatch is also a fourth blue — #1a57db, one hex digit off the accent.

screen: D — does the file read as one product
finding: Not yet. The shared components are real and correct — that part of the work holds up under measurement — but they cover 18.6% of the boards, and on the 81% they do not cover, the panel header, the drawer size, the group label and the button height still differ by module. The file reads as one product wherever the shell is drawn and as separate screens everywhere else.
evidence: What is genuinely unified, all measured: one Rail component set instanced 99 times with 0 hand copies and 42 wired buttons; one Settings nav row instanced 585 times with 573 wired and 12 correctly inert; four client-review masters instanced 39 times with 0 local copies on 1:6; 10/10 topbar save states truthful to their board names; text-style binding 40.6% -> 60.1%; six Inspector profiles converted to rows; page integrity clean at 29/0/0/0/2833. What is not: 99 of 533 boards carry the shell and 17 modules have none (D-R-16); the panel header is five different components (D-R-13); the drawer is four sizes (D-R-12); 407 group labels are hand-set while 537 identical ones bind a style (D-R-14); Button runs 28 and 32 within the same module (D-R-15); 100 text nodes are clipped (D-R-18); one #1c64f2 and 32 #3f83f8 survive on live boards (D-R-07); 33 titles are stranded at the old 14/21 (D-R-09). The tell is that a Settings board and a Media board cannot be compared at all — 638:2378 is a 1440x900 screen with rail, topbar and status bar; 144:2 is a 280x812 crop with none of them.
recommend: Three things, in this order, would change the answer more than anything else. 1) Build one Panel header component (title slot + optional back + optional icon pair, bound to ui/14 · panel title) and instance it in all thirteen panels — it is the element every user sees in every module and it is currently five components. 2) Settle the drawer size at 280x812 and redraw AI, Notifications and History onto it; that one decision also clears most of the History clipping in D-R-18 and the 33 stranded 14/21 titles in D-R-09, because all three failures are the same three modules. 3) Add one full-shell board per module — nine boards — so the rail, drawer and topbar can be compared by eye instead of by script; 81% of this file has never been seen next to the chrome it is supposed to share.
